# Feature: Run Ownership, Channel & Reconciliation

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-064
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_ui.md`

Today a run is "owned" by nothing durable. `LocalRunStore.createRunDirectory` writes a pid-only `.lock`
(`packages/core/src/workflow/replay/run-store.ts:163`). `RunOrchestrator.resume` sets the manifest to
`running` (`run-orchestrator.ts:388`). Nothing ever notices when that process dies, so a killed run
says "running" forever. Nothing else can watch a run while it executes either.

This feature gives every run an **exclusive, identity-verified owner** and a **live channel**:

- **Lease.** Every run directory (terminal CLI, detached worker, daemon) is claimed by exactly one
  process through an exclusive `lease.json`. The lease holds the owner's creation identity, the
  identities of the browsers it owns, its socket address and an unguessable run token.
- **Run socket.** The owner serves a per-run local socket. It has one framing grammar, size limits,
  token authentication, a version and capability handshake, bounded and prioritized outbound queues,
  and an atomic replay-to-live watermark. Any client can attach mid-run and see every event exactly
  once.
- **Detached worker.** An internal entry point (`apps/cli/dist/worker.js`) runs a
  `CommandInvocation` through FEAT-072's worker adapter. A single spawn helper starts it detached and
  shell-free on all three OSes.
- **Reconciliation.** When an owner is verifiably dead, an idempotent reconciler writes exactly one
  terminal result (`owner_lost`) and marks the manifest `interrupted`, separately from the
  evidence-based outcome (D7). It also reaps only the browsers whose identity it can prove.
- **Stop and guard.** A stop service tries a graceful `cancel`, then identity-verified forced
  termination, and always reconciles afterwards. `config data-dir` refuses while live leases or a
  host lock exist (D15).

**Business value.** On the CLI alone, `yantra list` stops showing dead runs as `running`. Leftover
Chrome processes from crashed runs are cleaned up safely. The app host (FEAT-065) can then launch
workers that outlive it, reattach after any crash, and show live progress without gaps. This
delivers the plan §14 promise that "killing any one process loses no committed local record" and
that each run ends with "exactly one honest terminal result".

**Task 1 is spike S2** (§8 Delivery milestones). Its findings can force an architecture change, so
TASK-002 onward do not start until its report is accepted.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

> `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does not exist. All state is filesystem-based (memory → Project
> Structure); there is no relational store. The history index (`index.db`) is only _updated_ through
> its existing `recordFromRunDir`, and its schema does not change.

### Entities & Attributes

- **RunLease** (`<runDir>/lease.json`; protocol schema `RunLease`, snake_case like other protocol
  schemas; owner-only file mode `0600`):
  - `schema_version` (literal `1`) — NOT NULL.
  - `run_id` (string) — must equal the run directory's name.
  - `owner` (`{pid: int > 0, start_token: string}`) — the claiming process's creation identity
    from `currentProcessIdentity()`. `start_token` may be `unknown`, and the liveness verdict is then
    `unknown`, never `dead`.
  - `origin` (`terminal | worker | daemon`) — who launched the run. FEAT-065 uses it to show
    CLI-launched runs without throttling them (D4).
  - `execution_class` (string) — the FEAT-062 registry `execution` value for the invocation
    (normally `run`).
  - `command` (string[]) — the command path, for example `["research"]`. Display only.
  - `owned_browsers` (array of `{pid, start_token, recorded_at}`) — Chrome processes this run spawned
    and has not yet proved exited. An entry is added as soon as a child handle exists and removed only
    after the supervisor proves the exit.
  - `socket` (`{kind: 'unix' | 'pipe', address: string}`) — the run socket address.
  - `run_token` (string, 43-character base64url of 32 random bytes) — the secret that authenticates
    run-socket clients. It is never logged, never sent to the model, and never served to the app.
  - `channel_version` (int) — the highest channel version the owner speaks (D17). It lets a host
    decide "live view unavailable" before connecting.
  - `yantra_version` (string) — for the D17 message "Started by Yantra <version>…".
  - `log_seq_at_claim` (int ≥ 0) — the last committed `run-events.jsonl` `seq` when this lease was
    claimed. It marks the ownership epoch, so a reconciler only looks for a terminal event _after_
    this claim. This matters for a resumed run whose earlier execution already ended.
  - `claimed_at` (ISO-8601) and `heartbeat_at` (ISO-8601) — the owner rewrites `heartbeat_at`
    every 5 s.
    > **Amended by spike S2 RC2** (accepted 2026-11-09): the lease is immutable after its `link` claim. `heartbeat_at` is dropped (liveness comes from creation identity and the socket heartbeat), and `owned_browsers` is not stored here: owned-browser identities live in the append-only `<runDir>/owned-browsers.jsonl` (`{op: 'spawned' | 'exited', pid, start_token, at}`, owner-only), folded by readers that ignore a trailing partial line.
- **ExecutionState** (protocol enum, plan §6 "Protocol additions"): exactly one value,
  `interrupted`. It is absent for every execution that ended on its own, so the enum has no dead
  values.
- **RunManifest extension** (`packages/core/src/workflow/replay/types.ts`):
  - `executionState?: ExecutionState` — set only by the reconciler, and cleared when a resume takes
    over the run.
  - > **RESOLVED (naming, user 2026-11-09: "be consistent across the app"):** the field is
    > **`executionState`**, because every top-level `RunManifest` key on disk is camelCase (`runId`,
    > `taskOutcome`, `terminationReason`, `runKind`). Protocol-owned schemas (lease, channel
    > messages, read views) stay snake_case. The plan and FEAT-066's manifest references now say
    > `executionState` too.
- **Run channel messages** (protocol schema `RunChannelMessage`; frame type `0x01`, UTF-8 JSON, at
  most 1 MiB; discriminated by `type`):
  - **client → owner:**
    - `hello {token, channel_version, capabilities: string[], client_kind: 'host' | 'cli' | 'test'}`
      — must be the first frame, at most 16 KiB, within 5 s of connecting;
    - `subscribe {from_seq}`;
    - `cancel {}`;
    - `ping {}`.
  - **owner → client:**
    - `hello_ok {channel_version, supported: {min, max}, capabilities: string[], run_id}`;
    - `hello_incompatible {supported: {min, max}, yantra_version}`, after which the connection
      closes;
    - `event {seq, event: RunEvent}`;
    - `event_oversize {seq}` — a placeholder for a single event whose encoding exceeds 1 MiB, so
      clients see no `seq` gap;
    - `heartbeat {at}`;
    - `cancel_ack {already_cancelling: boolean, honored: boolean}` — `honored` is `false` when the
      running handler does not honor an abort signal (FEAT-072 `honorsAbort`; today only `do` and
      `doctor --agent-smoke` do). The run then continues, and a stopper goes straight to forced
      termination (TASK-011);
    - `error {code: 'unsupported' | 'bad_request' | 'overflow', message}`.
  - **Extensibility.** Capabilities are strings, and unknown message `type`s parse as `{type:
string}` passthrough. FEAT-068 adds `intervention.answer` and `attendance`; FEAT-069 adds
    `frames.start/stop`, `frame.ack` and `frames.cleared` and the type `0x02` producer. None of them
    needs a channel-version bump. FEAT-064 advertises only `events` and `cancel`.
- **Frame** (wire grammar, plan §6):
  - layout: `[type: u8][length: u32 BE][payload]`;
  - type `0x01`: JSON, at most 1 MiB;
  - type `0x02`: screencast frame, at most 4 MiB, with payload `[meta_len: u16 BE][meta JSON][JPEG
bytes]`;
  - any other type, or any length over its type's limit, closes the connection.
- **WorkerLaunch** (`<launchDir>/<invocation_id>.launch.json`, owner-only and exclusively created by
  the spawner):
  - `schema_version` (literal `1`);
  - `invocation` (FEAT-062 `CommandInvocation {invocation_id, path, argv, cwd}`);
  - `run_id?` — preallocated by FEAT-065's slot reservation (D11);
  - `result_path` — an absolute path.

  User text such as goals therefore never appears in a process argument list.

- **WorkerResult** (`result_path`, atomically written once by the worker): `{schema_version: 1,
invocation_id, run_id?, outcome}`. `outcome` is FEAT-072's result transport shape, either `result
{exit_code, envelope}` or `error {exit_code, code, message, remediation}`.
- **reconcile.lock** (`<runDir>/reconcile.lock`) — a transient `proper-lockfile` lock with stale
  reclaim, held only during reconciliation or a resume takeover.

### Relationships

- Run directory 1:0..1 RunLease. At most one live lease exists per run directory, enforced by
  exclusive create.
- RunLease 1:N owned browser identities, embedded.
- RunLease 1:1 run socket (address and token in the lease). A socket N:M clients, each with its own
  outbound queues.
- Run directory 1:N ownership epochs. Each epoch is one lease claim (original run plus each resume),
  bounded in `run-events.jsonl` by `log_seq_at_claim`. Each epoch has **exactly one** terminal
  `run_outcome`.
- WorkerLaunch 1:1 WorkerResult 1:0..1 run directory.

### Indexes & Constraints

- **Exclusive publication.** A lease is published by writing a unique temp file (FEAT-072 helper,
  `<file>.<pid>.<random>.tmp`) and then calling `link(temp, lease.json)`. That fails with `EEXIST`
  if a lease exists, so a reader never sees a partial lease. Updates by the owner are temp-then-
  rename, retried on Windows `EPERM`/`EBUSY`.
- **Write ordering invariants:**
  1. the lease is claimed **before** the manifest says `running`;
  2. the terminal event **and** the terminal manifest are flushed **before** `lease.json` is removed.

  Hence a `running` manifest with no lease and no legacy `.lock` can only mean a dead owner.

- **Liveness** is decided only by `ProcessLivenessProbe.check(identity)` (creation identity), never
  by PID existence alone or by age. `unknown` is never treated as `dead`.

## 4. Dependencies

- **FEAT-063 Unified Run-Event Stream (hard).** This feature needs, by contract (plan §8 "Event log
  contract"):
  - the `RunEvent` union with `run_outcome` and `artifact_saved`;
  - the `owner_lost` `TerminationReason` variant with its fixtures;
  - a `run-events.jsonl` writer exposing:
    - the last committed `seq`;
    - a persist-before-publish committed-event listener;
    - flush;
    - open-for-append-after-tail-recovery, which the reconciler uses;
  - a reader that streams events in a `seq` range and ignores a trailing partial line.

  If the merged names differ, adapt at the call sites; do not duplicate the writer.

- **FEAT-072 Handler Seams, Receipts & Locks (hard for TASK-008 and TASK-012):**
  - the worker adapter and its result transport shape;
  - the handler abort-signal dependency, which `cancel` drives;
  - the unique-temp-file atomic write helper (a fixed `<path>.tmp` is a lint error);
  - the core lock conventions.
- **FEAT-062 Command Registry (hard for TASK-012):** the `CommandInvocation` schema and
  `parse`, and the registry lookup of an invocation's option-dependent `execution` class.
- **Spike S2 (TASK-001)** gates TASK-002 to TASK-014.
- **Existing modules, reused rather than re-implemented:**
  - `browser/process-identity.ts`: `currentProcessIdentity`, `NodeProcessLivenessProbe`,
    `UNKNOWN_START_TOKEN`;
  - `browser/process-lifecycle.ts`: `NodeProcessTreeTerminator`, `BrowserProcessSupervisor`;
  - `proper-lockfile`, already a core dependency;
  - `index-db/history-store.ts` `recordFromRunDir`;
  - `scheduler/daemon-lock.ts` `FileDaemonLock.probe()`, kept in the guard.
- **New third-party dependencies: none.** The feature uses `node:net`, `node:crypto`,
  `node:child_process` and `node:fs` only.
- **Downstream consumers (not built here):**
  - FEAT-065: host start calls `reconcileAll`; the host writes `WorkerLaunch`, supplies the
    invocation-claim start gate, and owns `host.lock`;
  - FEAT-067: Stop calls `stopRun`; the run screen uses `RunChannelClient` states;
  - FEAT-068: registers intervention and attendance handlers;
  - FEAT-069: frame producer and frame control handlers;
  - FEAT-071: Health lists `listPossibleOrphans()`.

## 5. Implementation Tasks

### TASK-001: Spike S2 — detached worker and recovery on Windows, macOS and Linux

- [ ] **Implementation**: Build a throwaway prototype in `e2e/spikes/s2-worker-recovery/`, using
      only `node:*`. Run it on all three OSes through a temporary `workflow_dispatch` CI job. Measure and
      record each scenario in `spike_s2_report.md`, with OS, Node version, pass or fail, timings and
      surprises.
  1. **Detached spawn.** `spawn(process.execPath, [worker], {detached: true, shell: false, stdio:
'ignore', windowsHide: true})` plus `unref()`. - Does the worker survive the parent's normal exit, a `SIGKILL`/`taskkill /F` of the parent,
     and closing the launching terminal? - On Windows, does the worker survive when the parent is inside a Job object with
     kill-on-close (VS Code terminal, Windows Terminal)? Node does not expose
     `CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB`, so document any mitigation.
  2. **Run socket.**
     - A Unix socket in a 0700 directory: measure path length against the macOS limit for a deep
       `YANTRA_HOME`, and test the `os.tmpdir()` fallback.
     - A Windows named pipe with a random name.
     - Token-first auth: an unauthenticated client gets no bytes.
     - Fragmented and coalesced frames.
  3. **Host death and reattach.** Kill the "host" mid-stream, start a new one, read the lease,
     reconnect, replay from `from_seq` while the worker keeps emitting, and check for no gap and no
     duplicate.
  4. **Approval across reconnect.** A toy pending item answered after a reconnect; a duplicate
     answer gets `already_decided`. This is only a prototype of the D12 shape, which FEAT-068 owns.
  5. **Orphan cleanup.**
     - Kill the worker while it owns a real Chrome launched through `puppeteer-core`.
     - Verify Chrome survives on POSIX (process group) and dies with `taskkill /T` on Windows.
     - Reap by `readStartToken` identity.
     - Forge a reused-PID identity and confirm it is not killed.
  6. **Identity cost.** Measure the latency of `currentProcessIdentity()` (Windows PowerShell CIM),
     and whether lease temp-then-rename hits `EPERM`/`EBUSY` while a reader holds the file open on
     Windows.

  The report ends with a **verdict**: either "plan D3/D6/§6/§8 hold as written", or a list of
  required changes. Any required change is recorded in this spec as a `DEVIATION:` note, and
  TASK-002 onward wait for user confirmation.

> **Spike S2 outcome (2026-11-09, Windows only).** Verdict: plan D3/D6/§6/§8 hold in shape, with
> the changes below. **All four were ACCEPTED by the user on 2026-11-09** and override the task text
> they amend; each affected task carries an "Amended by RC#" pointer. Linux/macOS verification was
> **waived** by the user for now and is tracked in `.spec-lite/TODO.md`; TASK-014's cross-OS suite is
> the first place a POSIX difference would surface. Evidence: `spike_s2_report.md`.
>
> - **DEVIATION (RC1, TASK-012):** `spawnDetachedWorker` spawns through a short-lived trampoline
>   that starts the worker detached, reports its PID and exits, because `taskkill /T` of a live
>   host kills directly spawned workers on Windows. A host inside a `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE` Job
>   without `SILENT_BREAKAWAY_OK` still kills its workers (Node has no breakaway flag; WMI drops
>   the environment). That is an accepted, documented limitation.
> - **DEVIATION (RC2, §2 RunLease, TASK-004/008/009/010):** `lease.json` is immutable after its
>   `link` claim. There is no `heartbeat_at` rewrite, and `owned_browsers` moves to an append-only
>   `<runDir>/owned-browsers.jsonl` (`spawned`/`exited` lines). Reconciliation appends `exited`
>   rather than rewriting the lease, and takeover replaces the lease by unlink then `link` under
>   `reconcile.lock`. The reason: on Windows, rename over `lease.json` fails with `EPERM` while any
>   reader holds it open, even with `FILE_SHARE_DELETE`.
> - **DEVIATION (RC3, TASK-005/006/008):** `finish()` ends every channel connection and waits (≤ 1 s)
>   before releasing the lease. `RunChannelClient` reads `run-events.jsonl` from `lastSeq + 1` when
>   the connection closes before `run_outcome`. Without the drain, the terminal frame was lost to
>   live clients in 3 of 3 runs.
> - **DEVIATION (RC4, TASK-009/010/013):** `NodeProcessLivenessProbe` short-circuits non-existent
>   PIDs with signal 0 and gains a batched `checkMany`, used by sweeps, `list` and the data-dir
>   guard. The reason: `identifyProcess` costs about 0.6–0.9 s per call on Windows.
> - **DEVIATION (spike CI):** the temporary three-OS job is `.github/workflows/spike-s2.yml`, run
>   on pushes to the feature branch, not a `workflow_dispatch` job in `ci.yml`. GitHub only
>   dispatches workflows whose default-branch copy declares the trigger. TASK-014 removes that file.

### TASK-003: Frame codec — one framing grammar with size limits

- [x] **Implementation**: Implement `packages/core/src/run-channel/frame-codec.ts`.
  - **`encodeJsonFrame(message)`** returns a `Buffer`. It throws `RunChannelFrameError` over 1 MiB.
  - **`encodeScreencastFrame(meta, jpeg)`** returns a `Buffer`. It throws over 4 MiB or when the meta
    JSON exceeds `u16`.
  - **`FrameDecoder`** is a class with `push(chunk): DecodedFrame[]`.
    - It accumulates across chunk boundaries (fragmentation) and returns several frames from one
      chunk (coalescing).
    - It validates the type byte and length **before** buffering the payload, so an oversized
      length is rejected without allocating it.
    - It returns `{kind: 'fatal', reason}` on an unknown type, an over-limit length, malformed UTF-8
      or JSON, or a `meta_len` larger than the payload. The caller then closes the connection.
    - It takes an optional per-state limit, used for the 16 KiB `hello` limit.

  - three frames coalesced in one chunk;
  - a frame split across the 5-byte header boundary;
  - type `0x03` is fatal;
  - a JSON length of 1 MiB + 1 is fatal without allocating the payload (assert the buffered bytes
    stay ≤ 5);
  - a screencast length of 4 MiB + 1 is fatal;
  - invalid UTF-8 and truncated JSON are fatal;
  - `meta_len` greater than the payload is fatal;
  - a hello-state limit of 16 KiB is enforced;

### TASK-005: Authenticated run socket with version and capability handshake

> **Amended by spike S2** (accepted 2026-11-09): RC3 (the server exposes a bounded graceful close that ends every connection before `finish()` releases the lease). See the TASK-001 notes and `spike_s2_report.md` → Required changes.

- [x] **Implementation**:
  - **`socket-address.ts`.** `allocateSocketAddress()` returns `{kind: 'unix', address:
<socketsRoot>/<random 24 hex>.sock}` or `{kind: 'pipe', address: \\.\pipe\yantra-<random 32
hex>}`. A stale Unix socket file at the address is unlinked only when its path is inside
    `socketsRoot()`.
  - **`RunChannelServer`** (`server.ts`), built on `node:net`.
    - `listen()` records the address into the lease before `RunOwnershipSession.open` returns.
    - **Per connection:**
      1. Start a 5 s hello deadline and decode with the 16 KiB hello limit.
      2. The first frame must be a JSON `hello`. Any other frame, a wrong token (`timingSafeEqual`
         over equal-length buffers; a length mismatch counts as wrong), or the deadline expiring
         destroys the socket **with zero bytes written**.
      3. On a valid token, negotiate `min(client.channel_version, CHANNEL_VERSION)`. If it falls
         outside `SUPPORTED_CHANNEL_VERSIONS`, send `hello_incompatible` and close.
      4. Otherwise reply `hello_ok` with the capability intersection.
    - **Handler registry.** `register(type, capability, handler)`. A known but unregistered `type`
      gets `error{unsupported}` and the connection stays open; malformed JSON closes it.
    - **Logging.** `channel_attached` and `channel_detached` go to the injected `Logger` with
      `client_kind`, negotiated version and duration. The token and the address are never logged.
  - **`RunChannelClient`** (`client.ts`).
    - `connect(lease)` sends `hello` and resolves to one of:
      - `{state: 'attached', capabilities}`;
      - `{state: 'live_unavailable', ownerVersion}`, when the owner sends `hello_incompatible` or
        the lease's `channel_version` is outside the client's range. In that case the client does
        not connect at all, and never sends `cancel`;
      - `{state: 'unreachable'}`.
- [x] **Unit Tests** (`server.spec.ts`, `client.spec.ts`, over real `node:net` sockets in a temp
      directory or pipe):
  - **Unauthenticated clients get nothing:**
    - no hello within 5 s (injected timer) means the socket closes and the client received 0 bytes;
    - a wrong token means 0 bytes and a close;
    - a token of a different length means 0 bytes;
    - a non-hello first frame means 0 bytes;
    - a 17 KiB first frame closes before buffering;
    - a garbage type byte closes.
  - A valid hello gets `hello_ok` with the capability intersection.
  - A client at `channel_version` 2 against server max 1 negotiates 1. A client at min 2 gets
    `hello_incompatible`.
  - **Previous-version fixture:** a fake owner advertising `{min: 0, max: 0}` leads
    `RunChannelClient` to report `live_unavailable`, and the client sends no `cancel` (assert the
    bytes the fake received).
  - An unregistered `intervention.answer` gets `error{unsupported}` and the connection survives.
  - A canary `run_token` never appears in the captured logger output.
- [x] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for architecture (run socket and
      handshake) and safety and privacy (token-first authentication, Unix socket directory permissions,
      named pipes on Windows).

### TASK-006: Atomic replay-to-live subscription with gap-free reconnect

> **Amended by spike S2** (accepted 2026-11-09): RC3 (on a close before `run_outcome`, the client reads `run-events.jsonl` from `lastSeq + 1` before reconnecting or reporting `unreachable`). See the TASK-001 notes and `spike_s2_report.md` → Required changes.

- [x] **Implementation**:
  - **Server, on `subscribe {from_seq}`.** All steps run on the owner's event loop (plan §8):
    1. register a per-connection buffering listener on the FEAT-063 committed-event listener;
    2. read the watermark `W` = last committed `seq`;
    3. stream file events `from_seq..W` with the FEAT-063 range reader. Streaming is **paced by
       socket drain** and is not counted against the 8 MiB live bound, so a 50,000-event replay
       never overflows;
    4. flush buffered events with `seq > W`, in order;
    5. switch to live forwarding.

    Further rules:
    - An event whose JSON frame would exceed 1 MiB is sent as `event_oversize {seq}`.
    - A second `subscribe` on the same connection restarts from its own `from_seq`.
    - Persist-before-publish is inherited: the listener fires only for committed events.

  - **Client.**
    - Dedupe by `seq`. It never delivers a `seq` ≤ the last delivered one, and it surfaces an
      internal `gap` diagnostic if one is ever seen. That should never happen; tests assert it.
    - `reconnect()` uses exponential backoff (250 ms → 5 s cap), re-reads the lease (a resumed run
      has a new token and address), and resubscribes with `from_seq = lastSeq + 1`.
    - `onEvent(listener)` and a `useSyncExternalStore`-friendly `getSnapshot()` of `lastSeq` and
      state.

- [x] **Unit Tests**:
  - Use a fake FEAT-063 log (an in-memory committed listener plus a range reader) and also the real
    writer once it is available.
  - **Gap-free attach:**
    - a client subscribing at `from_seq = 0` after 1,000 events receives 1..1,000 then live events;
    - **emit during replay:** the writer emits 500 events while the replay of 10,000 streams, and
      the client receives exactly 1..10,500, strictly increasing, with no duplicates;
    - a second client attaching mid-run sees the same sequence;
    - disconnecting at seq 400 and reconnecting with `from_seq = 401` gives no gaps or duplicates.
  - **Replay pacing and limits:**
    - a 50,000-event replay with a paused reader socket does not grow the live queue past its
      bound;
    - an oversize event yields `event_oversize` with the right `seq`;
    - a trailing partial line in the file is not delivered;
    - `from_seq` beyond `W` goes straight to live.
- [x] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for architecture (the event log
      contract and the replay-to-live watermark).
- **Verify**: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run tests/run-channel/server.spec.ts
tests/run-channel/client.spec.ts` passes.

### TASK-007: Bounded, prioritized outbound queues, backpressure and heartbeat

- [x] **Implementation**:
  - **`outbound-queues.ts`.** Each connection has two queues.
    - **Event queue:** control and event JSON frames, FIFO, bounded at 8 MiB of encoded bytes.
      Overflow sends one best-effort `error{overflow}` and destroys **that** connection only. The
      client reconnects and replays from the file, so nothing is lost.
    - **Frame queue:** a single slot; a newer type `0x02` frame replaces an unsent one.
    - **Writer loop:**
      - always drains the event queue before taking the frame slot;
      - honors `socket.write()` returning `false` by awaiting `drain`;
      - never awaits inside the publish path. `enqueue` is synchronous, so a slow socket cannot
        block the owner's event loop or other clients.
  - **Server.**
    - Fans out to every connection's event queue.
    - Exposes `publishFrame(meta, jpeg)` for FEAT-069. It is exercised here with synthetic frames
      only.
    - Sends `heartbeat {at}` every 5 s per connection, `unref`ed.
  - **Client.** Moves to state `not_responding` after 30 s with no frame of any kind (injected clock),
    logs it once, and returns to `attached` on the next frame.
  - All thresholds live in `run-ownership/constants.ts`: heartbeat 5 s, not-responding 30 s, queue
    bound 8 MiB, stop grace 10 s and hello deadline 5 s. They are open questions in plan §15, so they
    live in one place.
- [x] **Unit Tests** (`outbound-queues.spec.ts`, `server.spec.ts`):
  - **Prioritization:** with 20 queued 3 MiB frames and a control message, the control message is
    written before any frame.
  - **Slow-client isolation:**
    - a client that stops reading overflows at 8 MiB and is disconnected;
    - a second, fast client on the same server receives every event with p95 enqueue-to-write under
      50 ms. Assert ordering and that there is no stall over 100 ms on a stepped clock where
      possible.
  - **Frames:** a stalled frame acknowledgement does not delay control traffic (a `cancel_ack` is
    still delivered), and the frame slot holds only the newest frame (assert the dropped count).
  - **Backpressure:** an injected `write() → false` waits for `drain`.
  - **Heartbeat:** there is one heartbeat per 5 s on an injected clock. The client flips to
    `not_responding` at exactly 30 s and back on the next heartbeat.
- [x] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for architecture (queues,
      backpressure and liveness thresholds).
- **Verify**: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run tests/run-channel` passes. The e2e slow-client case
  in TASK-014 confirms it with real processes.
- **Depends on**: TASK-005

### TASK-009: Reconciler — exactly one terminal result for a dead owner, identity-verified browser reaping

> **Amended by spike S2** (accepted 2026-11-09): RC2 (step 7 appends `exited` lines and never rewrites the lease; owned browsers are read from `owned-browsers.jsonl`) and RC4 (verdicts through the batched probe). See the TASK-001 notes and `spike_s2_report.md` → Required changes.

  - **Dependencies:** `probe`, `terminator`, `clock`, `history` and `logger` are all injectable.
  - **Result:** a union of `no_lease | owner_alive | owner_unknown | busy | reconciled |
completed_by_evidence`.
  - **Algorithm** (plan §8), idempotent at every step: 1. **Lock.** Acquire `reconcile.lock` with `proper-lockfile` (`stale: 10_000`, `retries: 0`).
    Contention returns `busy`. 2. **Re-verify.** Read the lease. If it is absent, run the legacy path (below). Otherwise call
    `ownerVerdict`: - `alive` returns `owner_alive`; - `unknown` returns `owner_unknown` and changes nothing; - `dead` continues. A reused PID yields `dead` because its creation token differs, and that
    process is never signalled. 3. **Log.** Open the FEAT-063 writer in append-after-recovery mode, which truncates a partial
    tail. Look for a terminal `run_outcome` with `seq > lease.log_seq_at_claim`. - **If one exists:** the run finished before the owner died. Derive the outcome from it, do
    not append, and do not mark the run `interrupted` (`completed_by_evidence`). - **Else, if the manifest is already terminal** (status `completed`/`failed`/`aborted` with
    `taskOutcome`): append one `run_outcome` mirroring the manifest's outcome and reason
    (evidence `manifest`). - **Else:** append one `run_outcome` with `termination_reason: owner_lost` and the outcome
    from `result-evidence.ts`: - `partial` if a result was persisted: an `artifact_saved` of a result-bearing kind in
    this epoch, or a non-empty `brief.json`, `outputs.json` or document artifact; - otherwise `failed`; - **never** `aborted` (D7).

                 Flush.

              4. **Manifest.** Atomically patch it, preserving every unknown field because ask and research
                 manifests have their own shapes:
                 - `status` from `TASK_OUTCOME_TABLE[outcome].manifestStatus`;
                 - `taskOutcome`, `terminationReason`, `endedAt` (the last event time, else the reconcile
                   time) and `durationMs`;
                 - `executionState: 'interrupted'`, only in the `owner_lost` branch.

                 If no manifest exists, write a minimal `RunManifest` (`workflowName` = the lease `command`
                 joined, `runKind` derived from the command).

              5. **History.** Call `history.recordFromRunDir(runId)`. A failure is logged and is not fatal,
                 because the index is rebuildable.
              6. **Browsers.** For each `owned_browsers` entry, call `probe.check(identity)`:
                 - `alive`: re-check immediately before acting, then `terminator.terminate(pid)`, then confirm
                   `dead` (bounded wait);
                 - `dead`: drop the entry;
                 - `unknown`: **keep** the entry and never signal it.
              7. **Lease.** Remove `lease.json` only if no owned browser remains. Otherwise rewrite it with
                 only the uncertain entries; it is then a "possible orphan" record. Re-running the reconciler
                 later is a no-op for steps 3 to 5 and retries step 6.
              8. **Log and release.** Append `reconciled {by: 'host' | 'cli' | 'list' | 'stop', evidence:

        'event' | 'manifest' | 'owner_lost', reaped, uncertain}`to`runtime.jsonl`through

    `runtime-record.ts`. Release the lock.

  - **Legacy path** (no lease):
    - a `.lock` with a pid only: `processExists(pid) === false` reconciles. A live PID returns
      `owner_unknown`, because without a start token it cannot be verified;
    - a `running` manifest with neither file reconciles, by the ordering invariant.

### TASK-011: Stop service — graceful cancel, identity-verified forced termination, always reconcile

- [x] **Implementation**: Implement `stopRun({runDir, graceMs = 10_000}, deps)` in `stop-run.ts`.
  1. Read the lease. If there is none, return `not_running`.
  2. Connect with `RunChannelClient` and send `cancel`. If the owner is `live_unavailable` or
     `unreachable`, skip to step 4 without sending anything else.
  3. Wait up to `graceMs` for the lease to disappear (completion evidence flushed). If it does,
     return `stopped_gracefully` with the outcome read from the manifest. If the owner answered
     `cancel_ack {honored: false}`, skip the wait: that handler cannot stop cleanly.
  4. Call `ownerVerdict`:
     - `unknown` returns `stop_unverifiable` and never signals;
     - `dead` skips the signalling;
     - `alive` re-verifies and calls `NodeProcessTreeTerminator.terminate(owner.pid)` (forceful on
       Windows), then waits for a `dead` verdict.
  5. **Always** call `reconcileRun(runDir, {trigger: 'stop'})`. It reaps owned browsers by identity.
     Return `stopped_forcefully` with the reconcile result.

  This is a core service consumed by FEAT-065 and FEAT-067 (Stop). There is no new CLI command.

- [x] **Unit Tests** (`stop-run.spec.ts`, using a fake channel, probe, terminator and clock):
  - a cooperative owner removes its lease within the grace period, so the result is
    `stopped_gracefully` and the terminator is never called;
  - an unresponsive owner that ignores `cancel` is terminated after exactly 10 s (stepped clock),
    then reconciled;
  - an owner replying `honored: false` is terminated without waiting for the grace period, then
    reconciled;
  - an owner with an `unknown` identity gives `stop_unverifiable` with zero terminate calls;
  - a reused PID (`dead` verdict) is never signalled and is reconciled;
  - forced termination is always followed by reconciliation, even when `terminate` throws;
  - an incompatible owner is still stoppable through identity-verified termination.
- [x] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for architecture (the stop and
      forced-termination policy from the §8 reliability matrix).
- **Verify**: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run tests/run-ownership/stop-run.spec.ts` passes. The
  TASK-014 e2e covers real processes.
- **Depends on**: TASK-006, TASK-009

### TASK-012: Detached worker entry point and the single cross-OS spawn helper

> **Amended by spike S2** (accepted 2026-11-09): RC1 (`spawnDetachedWorker` spawns through a short-lived trampoline that reports the worker PID and exits; add a tree-kill/process-group survival test; document the kill-on-close Job limitation).   - **`apps/cli/src/worker.ts`**, built to `dist/worker.js` (add it to the build, not to `bin`).
    1. Parse exactly `--launch <abs path>`; anything else gives exit 1.
    2. Read and validate `WorkerLaunch`. Refuse a path outside `workerLaunchRoot()` unless
       `YANTRA_WORKER_LAUNCH_DIR` is set by tests.
    3. `process.chdir(invocation.cwd)`.
    4. Resolve the execution class through the FEAT-062 registry. Only `run`, `mutate` and
       `exclusive` are allowed. `in-process-secure`, `adapter`, `exemption` and `read` give a
       `WORKER_CLASS_REFUSED` error result with exit 1.
    5. Run the optional injected `WorkerStartGate`. The default is a no-op; FEAT-065 supplies the
       D11 invocation claim, and a gate refusal exits 0 with no side effects.
    6. Run the invocation through FEAT-072's worker adapter with `origin: 'worker'` and the
       preallocated `run_id` if present.
    7. Write `WorkerResult` atomically, exactly once, with mode `0600`, through
       `worker/result-sink.ts`. An uncaught error is caught at the entry, written as an `error`
       result, and exits 2.
    8. Set `process.exitCode`. If handles remain 5 s after the result is written, the entry (never a
       handler) hard-exits as a backstop.
  - **`apps/cli/src/worker/spawn.ts`: `spawnDetachedWorker({launch, env, nodePath =
process.execPath, workerPath})`.** 1. Exclusively create the launch file (`wx`, `0600`) in `launch.dir`. 2. Call `spawn(nodePath, [workerPath, '--launch', file], {cwd: invocation.cwd, env, detached:
true, shell: false, stdio: 'ignore', windowsHide: true})`, then `child.unref()`. 3. Return `{pid, identity}`, with the identity captured through `identifyProcess`.

                                                                                        Apply any mitigation the S2 report requires, for example Job-object breakaway on Windows.

### TASK-014: Cross-OS acceptance suite with real processes

- [ ] **Implementation**: Add `e2e/run-ownership.spec.ts`, tagged `@no-llm`, plus fixtures in

      (memory → Testing). Each case gets its own timeout for real-process work. Remove the temporary
      spike CI job from TASK-001.
  - **Killed run.** Start a real `yantra research --no-llm` against a local fixture server and kill
    it hard (`SIGKILL`, or `taskkill /F` without `/T` so Chrome is orphaned). Then run
    `yantra list --json` from **three concurrent processes**. Expected:
    - exactly one `run_outcome` line with `owner_lost`;
    - the manifest is `interrupted`;
    - the orphaned Chrome is gone, verified by identity;
    - the lease is removed.
  - **Reused PID.** A lease forged with a live unrelated process's PID and a wrong start token: the
    process survives and the run reconciles.
  - **Uncertain browser.** The lease names a live process with an `unknown` start token, through a
    test probe seam in the CLI test build: never killed, listed by `listPossibleOrphans`.
  - **Second client.** `fake-owner.mjs` emits continuously. A client attaches mid-run and replays
    while events are emitted, with no gaps and no duplicates. Kill and reattach it, then compare
    against the `run-events.jsonl` contents.
  - **Slow client.** `slow-client.mjs` stops reading and a second client keeps flowing. The slow
    client is dropped on overflow, then reconnects and replays to parity.
  - **Unauthenticated.** A raw socket connect with no or a wrong token receives 0 bytes.
  - **Previous version.** Against `channel-v0-server.mjs`, the client yields `live_unavailable`, and
    the fixture process continues and exits 0 on its own schedule.
  - **Stop.** `stopRun` on a cooperative `fake-owner.mjs` (honors cancel) is graceful. On a fixture
    that acknowledges but ignores abort, it terminates after 10 s and reconciles. On a real
    `research --no-llm` run (`honored: false`), it terminates at once and reconciles to
    `owner_lost`.
  - **Worker survival.** `spawnDetachedWorker` runs a `research --no-llm` from a parent that exits
    at once; the run completes, and the `WorkerResult` exit code matches the manifest outcome.

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth.**
  - **Run socket.** Every connection must present the lease's `run_token` in its first frame, within
    5 s and at most 16 KiB. Unauthenticated clients are closed without a reply (TASK-005).
  - **Where the token lives.** Only in the owner-only `lease.json`: `0600` on POSIX; the Windows
    user-profile ACL, as plan §7 states. The token is never logged, never put in events or receipts,
    and never sent to the model or the app. FEAT-065 adds the denied-file rule for `lease.json` and
    `reconcile.lock`.
  - **Socket locations.** Unix socket directories are verified owner-only. Windows pipe names are
    unguessable.
- **Error handling.**
  - **Typed errors.** `RunLeaseHeldError` (`busy`, exit 3, names the holder), `RunOwnerUnverifiable
Error`, `RunChannelFrameError` and `RunOwnershipError`, all with safe, actionable context
    (memory → Coding Standards).
  - **Uncertainty.** Identity uncertainty always resolves to "do nothing destructive": no kill, no
    reconcile, and the lease is kept.
  - **Non-fatal failures.** Heartbeat write failures, history index updates and sweep errors are
    logged, not fatal.
  - **The reconciler** never writes `aborted`, never writes a second terminal result per epoch, and
    can be re-run after a crash at any step.
  - **Malformed input** closes the connection, without throwing into the run.
- **Logging.**
  - **Run owner logger** (agentic runs use `runtime.jsonl` through the existing runtime logger):
    `channel_attached` and `channel_detached` (client kind, negotiated version, duration). A
    `not_responding` transition is logged once, by the client.
  - **`reconciled`** goes to the reconciled run's `runtime.jsonl`, with trigger, evidence used,
    reaped count and uncertain count.
  - **Never logged:** individual heartbeats, tokens, socket addresses in shared logs, or launch file
    contents.
- **Concurrency and locks.**
  - **Exclusive claims.** The lease uses `link`-based create; the launch file uses `wx`.
  - **Reconcile lock.** `reconcile.lock` uses `proper-lockfile`, as `daemon-lock.ts` already does.
  - **Atomic writes.** All of them use FEAT-072's unique temp-file helper.
- **Compatibility.**
  - **Additive.** Existing run directories stay readable. `.lock` is no longer written but is still
    read for legacy reconciliation.
  - **Older executables** cannot read `owner_lost` (accepted, D7).
  - **Channel versions.** The channel starts at version 1. Any later bump keeps answering older
    clients with `hello_incompatible` rather than misbehaving (D17).
- **Privacy.**
  - The worker receives user text through an owner-only launch file, never through argv (TASK-012
    asserts the command line).
  - Screencast frames are not produced here. The frame queue only transports what FEAT-069 supplies,
    and nothing in this feature persists a type `0x02` payload.
- **Zero-LLM.** Leases, sockets and reconciliation make no model calls. Daemon runs keep their hard
  zero-LLM guarantee (memory → Architecture).
- **Paths.** Every new root (`socketsRoot`, `workerLaunchRoot`, `uiHostLockPath`) is defined in
  `packages/core/src/browser/paths.ts` (memory → Project Structure).
